factorRatings.note: The Stranger called the wood-fired pies 'up there with the best in the city,' praising a thin, chewy crust with blackened char and a standout taleggio-mushroom pie; The Infatuation likewise singled out a well-executed Margherita and called the meatballs the best in the city, framing the Queen Anne room as a small but reliable destination for last-minute group dinners.

Seattle Met described it as a 'no-frills throwback pizza bar where the pie is for real,' and The Stranger profiled it as a Brooklyn-imported, New York-style slice bar helmed by veteran baker John Montenegro under restaurateur Mark Fuller, set in the old Pellegrini's Italian Market space with pinball machines and a dive-bar vibe; West Seattle Blog covered its November 2017 opening.

The Seattle Times called the pizza at this hidden Post Alley bar 'pretty decent,' framing the appeal mainly around its grungy, old-Seattle brick-and-lumber room (a former screenwriters' hangout with scripts still on the shelves) and happy-hour drinks rather than the food itself.
